question: What are the three main structural divisions of the brain stem?
explanation: The brain stem is anatomically divided from top to bottom into the midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h1)

question: The brain stem connects the spinal cord to which higher brain structure?
explanation: The brain stem acts as a structural bridge linking the higher centers of the brain to the spinal cord. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h1)

question: How many pairs of cranial nerves have their cell groups located inside the brain stem?
explanation: Cranial nerves three through twelve originate or end in the brain stem nuclei. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h2)

question: A patient with a stroke in the medulla has trouble swallowing and has a weak tongue. Which group of cranial nerves is affected?
explanation: The medulla oblongata houses the lower cranial nerves that control swallowing, speech, and tongue movement. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h2)

question: Where do the main motor pathways cross over to the opposite side in the brain stem?
explanation: The pyramidal decussation happens in the lower medulla where motor nerve fibers cross to the opposite side. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h3)

question: Why do injuries in the brain stem often cause symptoms on the opposite side of the body?

options.A: Pressure builds up and pushes cerebrospinal fluid to the other hemisphere.
options.B: Swelling blocks blood supply to both sides equally.
options.C: Nerve tracts cross over the midline as they travel through.
options.D: The brain stem directly controls opposing muscle groups simultaneously.

explanation: Because nerve tracts cross over or decussate, damage to one side affects signals coming from the opposite side. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h3)

question: What is the main job of the Reticular Activating System in the brain stem?
explanation: The reticular activating system sends signals to the cortex to keep the brain awake and alert. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h4)

question: A patient falls into a deep coma after a severe injury to the back of the head affecting the brain stem. Which structure is most likely damaged?
explanation: Damage to the reticular formation stops arousal signals from reaching the cerebral cortex, leading to a loss of consciousness. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h4)

question: Which part of the brain stem contains the main centers that control breathing and heart rate?
explanation: The medulla oblongata houses the automatic control centers for heart rate and breathing. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h5)

question: A patient with a compressed brain stem has irregular breathing and unstable blood pressure. What is the most important nursing action?

options.A: Encourage deep breathing exercises every two hours
options.B: Prepare for immediate airway management and ventilatory support
options.C: Administer oral analgesics to lower intracranial pressure
options.D: Position the patient flat on their back without a pillow

explanation: Brain stem compression affects automatic breathing centers, making airway security and mechanical ventilation lifesaving priorities. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h5)

question: What is a key sign often seen in brain stem injuries that affect both cranial nerves and motor pathways?

options.A: Total loss of vision combined with complete lower body spasticity
options.B: Crossed signs with facial weakness on one side and body paralysis on the other
options.C: Uniform bilateral paralysis of all four limbs without facial involvement
options.D: Isolated sensory loss in the lower extremities only

explanation: Brain stem injuries often cause facial weakness on the same side and body paralysis on the opposite side, known as crossed signs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h6)

question: Which finding is most alarming when monitoring a patient with increased pressure inside the skull and a risk of brain stem herniation?

options.A: A slight increase in blood pressure after a painful dressing change
options.B: Gradual onset of nausea without actual vomiting episodes
options.C: Mild agitation and complaints of a dull frontal headache
options.D: A sudden change in the level of consciousness and unequal pupils

explanation: Changes in consciousness and unequal pupils show pressure on the brain stem and cranial nerve III, which is a medical emergency. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h6)
